note: #2767 item 9 (comment-looking text inside a Markdown link title masked as a real HTML comment): findHtmlCommentRanges previously treated every unterminated "<!--" (no matching "-->" anywhere later in the body) the same way regardless of position, masking from that point through end-of-body -- including a "<!--" sitting mid-line inside a link title's quoted text, which is ordinary prose there, never a real HTML comment or block opener. That swallowed the genuine, later "Maintainer decision (...)" marker entirely, failing both Check 7 verifiability and A4's autonomous_completion for an issue that actually has a valid resolved decision. An intermediate #3282 revision (masking evaluateAutonomousCompletion's own scanned corpus through the same pipeline, per that issue's Proposed Change #1) changed the symptom from a false autonomous_completion FAIL to a false PASS without touching the root cause. FIXED (#3282, Copilot/CodeRabbit review on PR #3413): findHtmlCommentRanges now only lets an unterminated opener extend through end-of-text when it sits at a CommonMark HTML-block type-2 opening position -- after stripping 0+ blockquote container markers and optionally one list-item marker (its own required padding bounded to 1-4 columns, a bare tab counted via the usual tab-stop rule), at most 3 more leading spaces precede the opener -- confirmed against GitHub's own renderer via `gh api markdown`, which renders this exact body's link title verbatim and the "Maintainer decision" line as an ordinary, visible paragraph (and separately confirms a genuine line-start, blockquote-nested, or list-item-opening unterminated opener still swallows the rest of the document, unaffected by this fix). A mid-line unterminated opener like this one is no longer masked at all, so both Check 7 and A4's autonomous_completion now correctly see the resolved-decision marker and pass.
